title: Haydn's Words to Mozart's Father
text:
By 1785 Joseph Haydn was the most celebrated composer in Europe, and Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, twenty four years younger, was a rising star in Vienna. The two had become friends and sometimes played string quartets together. Mozart had studied Haydn's quartets closely and spent more than two years writing a set of six of his own, which cost him unusual effort.

In February 1785 Mozart's father Leopold came to visit his son in Vienna. On one evening Haydn came to hear three of the new quartets. Leopold described the scene in a letter to his daughter: Haydn turned to him and said, "Before God and as an honest man I tell you that your son is the greatest composer known to me either in person or by name." Haydn praised his taste and his deep knowledge of composition. For a father who had devoted his life to his son's career, it was an extraordinary moment.

That autumn Mozart published the six quartets with an affectionate dedication to Haydn, calling them his children and entrusting them to his friend's care. When Mozart died in 1791, Haydn, then in London, was deeply grieved.
lesson: Praise a younger talent generously, even one who might outshine you. Recognizing greatness in others is a sign of strength, not a loss of standing.
people: Joseph Haydn, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Leopold Mozart
source: Leopold Mozart, letter to Nannerl Mozart, February 16, 1785; Mozart, dedication of the six "Haydn" quartets (September 1, 1785)
